topic: Non-firearm competitor gear for the Mammoth Sniper Challenge, comparing manufacturer claims against independent reviewers and practitioner experience. In scope: spotting and measuring gear (riflescopes and mounts, spotting scopes, rangefinders and binoculars, Kestrel wind meters, ballistic apps and calculators, data books and wrist coaches, night vision and thermal devices); shooting support (bipods, tripods, shooting bags); rucking and endurance gear (packs, boots, socks and foot care, hydration, trekking poles, knee and elbow pads, gloves, food and energy sources); clothing and protection (tactical clothing, rain and cold-weather layers, eye protection, holsters); and weather and survival gear (sleep systems, first aid kits, power banks and solar charging). Reviews of firearms and ammunition are excluded.
audience: Prospective Mammoth Sniper Challenge competitors who already shoot precision rifle recreationally and understand basic gear terminology, but have not yet competed in a multi-day team endurance event where every piece of gear is carried on foot
central_question: What gear is worth buying to succeed in the Mammoth Sniper Challenge, which gear is absolutely necessary and which is optional, and do independent tests and field experience support what the manufacturers claim?
